metadata.title: New type of bubbling solutions to a critical fractional Schrödinger equation with double potentials
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we study the following critical fractional Schrödinger equation: \begin{equation} (-\Delta)^s u+V(|y'|,y'')u=K(|y'|,y'')u^{\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}},\quad u>0,\quad y =(y',y'') \in \mathbb{R}^3\times\mathbb{R}^{n-3}, \qquad(0.1)\end{equation} where $n\geq 3$, $s\in(0,1)$, $V(|y'|,y'')$ and $K(|y'|,y'')$ are two bounded nonnegative potential functions. Under the conditions that $K(r,y'')$ has a stable critical point $(r_0,y_0'')$ with $r_0>0$, $K(r_0,y_0'')>0$ and $V(r_0,y_0'')>0$, we prove that equation (0.1) has a new type of infinitely many solutions that concentrate at points lying on the top and the bottom of a cylinder. In particular, the bubble solutions can concentrate at a pair of symmetric points with respect to the origin. Our proofs make use of a modified finite-dimensional reduction method and local Pohozaev identities.

metadata.title: Triangulation, Volume, and Symmetries of a Dihedral Group Analogue of the Permutohedron
metadata.abstract: We study an analogue of the permutohedron for the dihedral group, which we call the dihedral permutohedron. We determine the facet structure of the dihedral permutohedron, use the facet structure to construct a triangulation, and determine a nice combinatorial formula for the volume of the dihedral permutohedron. Lastly, we find a family of interesting unimodular affine symmetries of the odd dihedral permutohedron.

metadata.title: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
metadata.abstract: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincaré expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori. The ensemble average supplies the sum over the solid tori, or more precisely over marked presentations with fixed base genus, number of fibers and integer Seifert invariant. The resulting sum converges absolutely and is a polynomial in the components of the vector-valued Eisenstein series. When all the boundary tori share a single modulus, the average acquires connected corrections, which we identify with wormholes gluing the core to itself; for two boundary tori, the terms with rational Lagrangian sublattices of the Siegel-Eisenstein series are realized by wormholes containing an exceptional fiber. After reduction along the fiber, the construction closely parallels the two-dimensional topological gravity of Marolf and Maxfield, with the base of the fibration playing the role of their spacetime. We also discuss Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with torus boundary, non-orientable bases, and the surgery formula. Our results suggest that modularity could be an organizing principle in the summation of geometries in quantum gravity.

metadata.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration
metadata.abstract: Deep neural networks extract powerful latent representations from images, enabling fast and efficient downstream analysis. However, these latent spaces lack explicit geometric structure, leading to possibly poor interpolation fidelity and misleading extrapolation. Latent interpolation techniques assume symmetric transition costs which are often not the case for real world data. Their symmetric nature cannot capture directional processes, such as disease progression, where certain transitions are impossible (e.g. tumor growth dynamics or cognitive improvement in Alzheimer's disease). Although Riemannian metrics extend Euclidean geometry by incorporating curvature, they remain symmetric. We show that understanding asymmetry and not curvature alone directly addresses these problems. To do so we propose a new Finsler-Randers metric learning framework. It incorporates direction-dependent distances, thus enabling the computation of trajectories respecting monotonic sequential constraints. We demonstrate its potential for interpolation and extrapolation on controlled cross-sectional datasets.

metadata.title: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 32-35 and 37-39
metadata.abstract: We show that the kissing numbers in dimensions 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38 and 39 are at least 352320, 370240, 390980, 415308, 499816, 605322 and 768916, improving the previous bounds 347584, 364736, 384836, 409676, 498024, 591900 and 763668. Except in dimension 38, the configurations are those of Edel, Rains and Sloane with new binary constant-weight codes of weight 8 and minimum distance 8 in the middle layer; each additional word adds 128 points. In dimension 38 we add 6855 antipodal pairs of vectors of the second shell of the Leech lattice to the empty equator of Kravatskiy's 591612-point configuration, where 144 pairs were known; this is an independent set problem in a regular graph of degree 11178 on 8386560 vertices. The codes and lines were found by local search, and all configurations were checked pair by pair in exact integer arithmetic.

metadata.title: The nonexistence of nine-point crescent configurations
metadata.abstract: A planar crescent configuration consists of $n$ points, no three collinear and no four concyclic, whose distinct distances have multiplicities $1,2,\ldots,n-1$. We prove by exact computation that no such configuration exists for $n=9$. The three pairs carrying the two least frequent distances yield a six-point subset with at most six distances. Rational linear algebra on quartic polynomials separates the possible six-point distance patterns into those with certified finite lists of normalized distance tuples and a residual family. Compatibility of overlapping subsets forces at least one core into the first family, without classifying the residual realizations. The remaining three points are then obtained by rational constructions over the field of the squared core distances. The multiplication matrices used to enumerate the core distances have order at most twelve. Exhaustive label assignments and exact algebraic comparisons exclude all remaining extensions.

metadata.title: Grid triples, link cobordisms in $\CPbar$ and the computation of Heegaard-Floer TQFT
metadata.abstract: We give a combinatorial description of the Heegaard--Floer link-cobordism maps associated with pointed triple grid diagrams in the complement of three $4$-balls in complex projective plane with reverse orientation. Every contributing index-zero holomorphic triangle decomposes into Euclidean triangular sheets. We characterize the compatible collections of sheets that contribute by an explicit geometric separation criterion, expressed as a lattice-point test, and prove that each has mod-\(2\) count one. Individual sheets may wrap around the torus in the unblocked theory, whereas they are embedded in the blocked theory. In each fixed \(\SpinC\) structure, the map is determined by a finite enumeration. A difference number computed from the triangular regions determines the \(\SpinC\) structure of a Whitney triangle. Together with the topology of the associated surface, this gives an explicit formula for the absolute bigrading of each summand of the cobordism map. After basepoint reduction, the formula determines the Laurent monomial representing any nonzero map on the rank-one torsion-free two-variable knot Floer modules, yielding vanishing and ideal-containment criteria. We apply the construction to an affine family of grid links \(K(n;p,s)\), obtaining explicit cobordisms involving infinite families of torus knots and links, together with closed formulas for the bigradings of their distinguished grid states.

analysisBasis.abstract: We give a combinatorial description of the Heegaard--Floer link-cobordism maps associated with pointed triple grid diagrams in the complement of three $4$-balls in complex projective plane with reverse orientation. Every contributing index-zero holomorphic triangle decomposes into Euclidean triangular sheets. We characterize the compatible collections of sheets that contribute by an explicit geometric separation criterion, expressed as a lattice-point test, and prove that each has mod-\(2\) count one. Individual sheets may wrap around the torus in the unblocked theory, whereas they are embedded in the blocked theory. In each fixed \(\SpinC\) structure, the map is determined by a finite enumeration. A difference number computed from the triangular regions determines the \(\SpinC\) structure of a Whitney triangle. Together with the topology of the associated surface, this gives an explicit formula for the absolute bigrading of each summand of the cobordism map. After basepoint reduction, the formula determines the Laurent monomial representing any nonzero map on the rank-one torsion-free two-variable knot Floer modules, yielding vanishing and ideal-containment criteria. We apply the construction to an affine family of grid links \(K(n;p,s)\), obtaining explicit cobordisms involving infinite families of torus knots and links, together with closed formulas for the bigradings of their distinguished grid states.

metadata.title: Uniqueness of scalar-flat ALE Kähler metrics
metadata.abstract: We study uniqueness of scalar-flat Kähler metrics in a fixed Kähler class on an asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) Kähler manifold, assuming only differentiated $o(1)$ decay to a fixed Euclidean metric on the end. In complex dimension $n\geq2$, under suitable polynomial decay of the reference metric, we prove that the relative Mabuchi functional is finite, continuous, and convex along weak geodesics whose endpoint potentials satisfy $u=O(r^{-\gamma})$, $\gamma>2n-4$, together with the corresponding derivative estimates. Combining this convexity with the analysis of the Lichnerowicz operator in weighted spaces, we obtain uniqueness by a perturbation argument. Decay improvement and comparison of the asymptotic charts produce a global potential with the required decay for the difference of the two cohomologous scalar-flat Kähler forms. The argument also extends to asymptotically conical Kähler metrics approaching a fixed Ricci-flat Kähler cone under prescribed decay assumptions.

metadata.title: Pure Spinor Factorization of Belinski-Zakharov Solitons and Regular Gravitational Instantons
metadata.abstract: We show that the Belinski-Zakharov soliton construction factorizes into signed Pfaffian tau-functions, revealing a pure-spinor description of the metric and its regularity conditions. We derive analytic restrictions on the integral rod data, prove uniqueness for the asymptotically flat balance problem at fixed rod structure and periods, and give a conditional criterion for global existence. Combining these results with exhaustive enumeration of the admissible data and rigorous existence certificates, we construct a catalogue of regular asymptotically flat solutions representing 356 rod-word classes through twelve turning points, and 52 isolated regular asymptotically locally flat solutions through eight turning points. Analytic positivity and smooth-completion results establish regularity beyond the finite numerical solve. Based on this catalogue, we investigate two organizations of the solution space: generalized rank-two root systems and compositions of simpler endpoint geometries. The endpoint composition rules reproduce exactly all retained asymptotically flat words through twelve turning points.

metadata.title: Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow
metadata.abstract: We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not Ricci-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in(0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton whose volume growth is subquadratic, in the sense that $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\Vol(B(p,r))/r^2=0$, has finite conjugate radius.

metadata.title: Combination Theorems and the Farrell--Jones Conjecture for Graph Products of Pairs
metadata.abstract: We study the Farrell--Jones conjecture for graph products of pairs and for fundamental groups of polyhedral products. We introduce a pair-deletion decomposition and a local notion of FJ-admissibility, and prove a vertexwise combination theorem for graph products of pairs. The criterion applies, in particular, to ordinary graph products, free-factor pairs, suitable normal pairs, and classes controlled by acylindrical Bass--Serre actions. For polyhedral products, we combine these results with their description by relative graph products and graph products of pairs. We also obtain bounds and exact computations for amenable category, together with applications to simplicial volume and Borel rigidity of closed aspherical polyhedral-product manifolds.

metadata.title: A surface-group action on real-hyperbolic space with no Cannon--Thurston map
metadata.abstract: We present discrete, faithful and purely loxodromic representations of a closed surface group of genus 431, and of a free group, into the group of isometries of a finite-dimensional real-hyperbolic space for which no Cannon--Thurston map exists. The construction combines three ingredients: the small-cancellation strategy employed by Baker--Riley to construct a subgroup of an ambient hyperbolic group with no Cannon--Thurston map, the realization of these groups by octagon complexes, and a theorem of Desgroseilliers--Haglund that supplies a convex cocompact faithful representation of the ambient hyperbolic group on a real-hyperbolic space. These examples admit ray Cannon--Thurston maps, as defined by Halder, Mahan Mj and Sardar.

metadata.title: Balance in Inequality: Testing the Physical Equilibrium, Precession, and Structural Stability of Magic Gems
metadata.abstract: A magic square exemplifies balance in inequality: its $n^2$ entries $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ are distinct, yet every row, column, and main diagonal sums to $\mu_n=n(n^2+1)/2$. Lifting centred grid cells into $\mathbb{R}^3$ as radial vectors $\mathbf{p}_{ij}(\lambda)=(x_j,y_i,\lambda z_{ij})$ and taking their convex hull---the Magic Gem $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$---asks: when does line-sum equality suffice for equilibrium in 3D, and when a nonlinear realization breaks balance, how can an opposing inequality restore it? We test this across all $880$ order-$4$ magic squares in four regimes. For radial spokes from $O$, natural lengths balance identically, while unit spokes break equilibrium on all $832$ non-associative squares in 3D and on all squares in 2D, where the ring-radius ratio $r_2/r_1=\sqrt{5}$ bounds the resultant below by the Pell convergent $9/4\approx\sqrt{5}$. By length--weight duality, balance is restored via tip weights $\mathbf{w}^*>\mathbf{0}$ on $S^2$ or power-law spoke scaling ($r^{\alpha^*}$ in 2D and $(\mathbf{V}_3)_z=0$ in 3D). In 3D rotation, equal point masses make every semi-magic square an axisymmetric top with spherical-top transition $\lambda_{\mathrm{iso}}=(n^2+1)^{-1/2}$, whereas entry masses $m_{ij}=s_{ij}$ expose the quadrupole $Q_{xy}=\sum z_{ij}x_jy_i$, triggering $180^\circ$ Dzhanibekov flips on $824$ squares. Passing to the uniform solid hull $\mathcal{G}_0(S)$ shifts the centroid off $O$ on $829$ squares; re-engaging the opposing core $\mathcal{G}_1(S)$ restores balance via two-density inclusions, nested wireframes, or the $K_{n^2}$ strut network, while all $880$ hulls unfold into non-overlapping nets with $f_0-1$ glue tabs. Finally, $\lambda=1/5$ stabilizes $74.5\%$ of facets on a table, and alternating $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ with its mirror twin $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(r^2\overline{S})=-\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ locks chiral blocks into a vertical tower.

analysisBasis.abstract: A magic square exemplifies balance in inequality: its $n^2$ entries $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ are distinct, yet every row, column, and main diagonal sums to $\mu_n=n(n^2+1)/2$. Lifting centred grid cells into $\mathbb{R}^3$ as radial vectors $\mathbf{p}_{ij}(\lambda)=(x_j,y_i,\lambda z_{ij})$ and taking their convex hull---the Magic Gem $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$---asks: when does line-sum equality suffice for equilibrium in 3D, and when a nonlinear realization breaks balance, how can an opposing inequality restore it? We test this across all $880$ order-$4$ magic squares in four regimes. For radial spokes from $O$, natural lengths balance identically, while unit spokes break equilibrium on all $832$ non-associative squares in 3D and on all squares in 2D, where the ring-radius ratio $r_2/r_1=\sqrt{5}$ bounds the resultant below by the Pell convergent $9/4\approx\sqrt{5}$. By length--weight duality, balance is restored via tip weights $\mathbf{w}^*>\mathbf{0}$ on $S^2$ or power-law spoke scaling ($r^{\alpha^*}$ in 2D and $(\mathbf{V}_3)_z=0$ in 3D). In 3D rotation, equal point masses make every semi-magic square an axisymmetric top with spherical-top transition $\lambda_{\mathrm{iso}}=(n^2+1)^{-1/2}$, whereas entry masses $m_{ij}=s_{ij}$ expose the quadrupole $Q_{xy}=\sum z_{ij}x_jy_i$, triggering $180^\circ$ Dzhanibekov flips on $824$ squares. Passing to the uniform solid hull $\mathcal{G}_0(S)$ shifts the centroid off $O$ on $829$ squares; re-engaging the opposing core $\mathcal{G}_1(S)$ restores balance via two-density inclusions, nested wireframes, or the $K_{n^2}$ strut network, while all $880$ hulls unfold into non-overlapping nets with $f_0-1$ glue tabs. Finally, $\lambda=1/5$ stabilizes $74.5\%$ of facets on a table, and alternating $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ with its mirror twin $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(r^2\overline{S})=-\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ locks chiral blocks into a vertical tower.

metadata.title: Universal bounds for decompositions of PL manifolds
metadata.abstract: The geometric dimension of a nonempty compact PL manifold $N$ is the smallest nonnegative integer $d$ for which $N$ admits a handle decomposition with all handles of index at most $d$. A PL filling of a compact PL manifold is a decomposition into compact codimension $0$ PL submanifolds, called sectors, with pairwise disjoint interiors and intersections described by standard local models. We advance Singhof's program of simplifying the sectors of a filling and their intersections. Specifically, for integers $m, \ell\ge 1$ and nonnegative integers $a_1\le\cdots\le a_\ell$, we prove that every closed PL $m$-manifold admits a filling into $\ell$ sectors whose nonempty $r$-fold intersections have geometric dimension at most $a_r$ for each $1\le r\le \ell$ if and only if \[ a_{\lambda_1}+\cdots+a_{\lambda_q}\ge m-\ell+1 \] for every partition $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_q=\ell$ into positive integers. Under the same inequalities, any prescribed $\ell$-sector filling of the boundary of a compact PL $m$-manifold extends to a filling with the corresponding relative handle index bounds. Necessity follows from the cup-product obstructions of Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. To prove sufficiency, we develop compatible handle trades that simplify intersections in increasing order of depth. For nondecreasing tuples of nonnegative integers, our theorem resolves the PL classification problem posed by Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. In particular, we obtain the bound $(2,2,4)$ for $3$-sector fillings in dimension $6$ and improve the $5$-sector bound $(1,2,3,3,4)$ of Rubinstein and Tillmann to $(1,2,2,3,4)$ in dimension $8$.

metadata.title: Overdetermined boundary problems for maximal graphs
metadata.abstract: We study overdetermined boundary problems for the maximal surface equation with zero Dirichlet data and constant nonzero Neumann data . For the exterior of a bounded domain with connected boundary in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$, we prove that such domain must be the complement of a ball and the solution is radial. In dimension two, we also show that a positive solution on a domain bounded by a properly embedded noncompact connected curve forces the domain to be a half-plane and the solution to be affine. The proofs combine the divergence structure of the equation with the induced geometry of maximal graphs.

metadata.title: Feynman Propagators on Exponentially Decaying Perturbations of Stationary Spacetimes with Compact Cauchy Surface
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we construct Feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetime with compact Cauchy surface. The propagators are defined as parametrices of the wave operator on exponentially weighted Sobolev spaces defined by complex contours $\Gamma$. We then apply this theory to the computation of indexes of Dirac operators using a continuous Wick-like rotation to relate it to the Riemannian case.

metadata.abstract: We prove that there are no proper biharmonic submanifolds with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field in a nonpositive space form, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. These results provide substantial support for Chen's conjecture and the generalized Chen's conjecture for hyperbolic space in higher codimensions.

metadata.title: Smooth and Topological Nonorientable Four-Genera of Low-Crossing Knots
metadata.abstract: We compare linking-form bounds with the smooth and locally flat nonorientable 4-genera of low-crossing knots. For every prime knot with at most 13 crossings whose Witt-level linking-form bound is at least 2, this bound equals both genera. We also exhibit 41 prime knots with 12 or 13 crossings that bound locally flat Möbius bands but no smooth ones, and whose smooth nonorientable 4-genus is 2. Our methods combine linking forms, Heegaard Floer correction terms and definite-lattice obstructions with explicit band constructions. They determine 3,300 of the 3,525 values left unknown in KnotInfo on 2 November 2026; the remaining 225 knots have range $[1,2]$. We obtain new lower bounds of 2 for 2,102 knots with 14 crossings and correct previously reported values for three knots with 11 crossings.

metadata.abstract: In this note, we begin with considering the simple one-dimensional field theory describing a single free particle on manifold, and apply the BRST formalism and BV quantization to this model following the standard procedures in physics. This note thus elucidates the physical origins and mechanisms of these mathematical results.

analysisBasis.abstract: In this note, we begin with considering the simple one-dimensional field theory describing a single free particle on manifold, and apply the BRST formalism and BV quantization to this model following the standard procedures in physics. Through calculations that, while not fully rigorous, have a more transparent physical interpretation, then subsequent geometric identifications, we recover the deformation quantization and algebraic index theorem on symplectic manifold. metadata.title: Pick-up sticks problems for exponential and Pareto distributions
metadata.abstract: We deal with the following two pick-up sticks problems: given an integer n greater than or equal to 3, we choose n sticks with independent random lengths from an exponential distribution or Pareto type I distribution, and we are interested in the probability that no three of them can be the sides of a triangle. In case of exponential distribution, this problem has been solved by other authors: the probability in question is equal to $n!/\big((F_3-1)(F_4-1)\cdots(F_{n+2}-1)\big)$, where $(F_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ is the sequence of Fibonacci numbers. We give a new, self-contained and detailed proof for this formula, which uses a different method compared to the earlier ones. In case of Pareto type I distribution, we derive new formulae for the corresponding probability.

metadata.title: Strong $G_2$-structures with torsion: a survey and new examples
metadata.abstract: This article has two main parts. The first consists of a brief survey of $G_2$-structures with torsion, namely $G_2$-structures admitting a $G_2$-connection with totally skew-symmetric torsion. We focus primarily on the strong condition that the associated torsion $3$-form is closed. We review their basic properties and their connections with the heterotic $G_2$ system, generalized geometry, and six-dimensional geometry. In the second part, we construct two complete cohomogeneity-one strong $G_2T$-structures on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3\times S^3$ with non-zero closed and co-closed characteristic torsion, and non-vanishing characteristic Ricci tensor. Both have an asymptotically cylindrical end; at the other end, the first is asymptotically conical (AC), with a torsion-free $G_2$ cone as its asymptotic model, while the second is asymptotically locally conical (ALC), with a constant-length circle bundle over a Calabi--Yau cone as its asymptotic model. We investigate the induced $SU(3)$-structures on their circle quotients and show that they are globally conformally almost Kähler and globally conformally Kähler, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these provide the first complete strong $G_2T$-structures whose underlying metrics are not locally Riemannian products.

metadata.title: Exotic Dehn twists on sums of 4-manifolds, nuclei, and exotic structures
metadata.abstract: For closed 4-manifolds $X_1, X_2$, we give a sufficient condition, in terms of the Seiberg-Witten invariants of $X_i$, for the Dehn twist on $X_1\#X_2$ along the neck to be smoothly nontrivial. This provides a broad generalization of the result of Kronheimer-Mrowka for $K3\#K3$. We also show that the boundary Dehn twists on the punctured connected sums of many pairs of elliptic surfaces are smoothly nontrivial. We also detect new examples of exotic Dehn twists along Seifert fibered 3-manifolds in elliptic surfaces. As a consequence, we exhibit a new phenomenon in which "exotic diffeomorphisms detect exotic smooth structures on 4-manifolds": the triviality of the boundary Dehn twist characterizes the standard nucleus $N(n)$ among the nuclei $N(n)_{p,q}$ homeomorphic to it, provided that $n\equiv0 \bmod 4$. These results are proved by computing the families Bauer-Furuta invariant for a new framing of the families Dirac index.

metadata.title: Finiteness properties of centralisers in $\mathrm{Out}(F_N)$ and automorphisms of free-by-cyclic groups
metadata.abstract: Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group. We prove that the centraliser of any element of $\mathrm{Out}(F)$ or $\mathrm{Aut}(F)$ is of type $\rm{VF}$. This relies on the construction of a new $\mathrm{Out}(M)$-invariant splitting of $M$, that enables us to reduce the proof of the above statements to the case where the outer class of $\varphi$ has finite order.

metadata.title: Unbounded total mean curvature with prescribed boundary metric
metadata.abstract: Bär has shown that a fixed boundary metric and a scalar-curvature lower bound do not generally bound total mean curvature from above. We extend this unboundedness to every smooth compact connected manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with nonempty boundary and every prescribed boundary metric, using scalar-flat metrics. While Bär's examples use warped products, our construction uses a nonzero cubic variation of total mean curvature near a flat product, followed by localization and conformal correction. We also construct arbitrarily $C^k$-small perturbations of the flat torical half-cylinder with nonnegative scalar curvature, unchanged boundary metric, an exact product end, and positive total boundary mean curvature.

analysisBasis.abstract: Bär has shown that a fixed boundary metric and a scalar-curvature lower bound do not generally bound total mean curvature from above. metadata.title: Hidden Symmetries of the Kepler Problem and Jacobi's Theorem
metadata.abstract: We present a geometric derivation of the hidden symmetries of the Kepler problem, combining a duality for central-force systems, obtained by interchanging positions and velocities, with a generalized form of Jacobi's theorem. Applied to the dual Kepler problem, this theorem identifies Kepler hodographs of prescribed energy with geodesics of a metric of constant curvature. After adjoining one point at infinity, the resulting geometry is complete. Its Killing vector fields induce a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries on the corresponding energy hypersurface. The distinguished point at infinity determines a canonical decomposition of the Killing algebra into two vector subspaces, whose associated Noether invariants recover angular momentum and the Runge-Lenz vector.

metadata.title: Pseudo-Einstein Structures on Links of Isolated Singularities
metadata.abstract: We study Jack Lee's conjecture that, for a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$, the condition $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{R})$ implies the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. For links of isolated singularities, we construct counterexamples in every odd dimension at least three, with $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_1(M)=0$. For isolated algebraic singularities of log canonical type and complex dimension at least three, we prove that the real Chern class condition is equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartierness of the canonical divisor, log canonicity, and the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. Finally, we construct a Du Bois threefold singularity whose link satisfies the real Chern class condition but admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. The initial versions of the proofs were generated with AI assistance and were subsequently revised and verified by the authors.

metadata.title: Curvature Estimates and Prescribed Curvature Problems for Sum Hessian Equations on Star-Shaped Hypersurfaces
metadata.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed star-shaped hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ and let $\eta=Hg-h$ be the first Newton transformation of its second fundamental form. For a fixed constant $\alpha>0$ and $2\le k\le n-1$, we study the prescribed sum Hessian curvature equation \[ \sigma_k(\lambda(\eta))+\alpha\sigma_{k-1}(\lambda(\eta))=f(X,\nu). \] Under the natural admissibility condition \[ \lambda(\eta)\in\Gamma_{k-1}\cap \{\lambda:\sigma_k(\lambda)+\alpha\sigma_{k-1}(\lambda)>0\}, \] we establish a global curvature estimate for closed star-shaped solutions with a general positive right-hand side depending on the position vector and the unit normal. A key point is that the sum Hessian operator is nonhomogeneous; the resulting lower-order term in the maximum-principle calculation is controlled by a partial curvature estimate. We also use the augmented-variable identity \[ \sigma_k(\lambda)+\alpha\sigma_{k-1}(\lambda) =\sigma_k(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n,\alpha) \] to recover the relevant ellipticity and concavity properties. As an application of the a priori estimates, we prove existence and uniqueness for the corresponding prescribed curvature problem under suitable spherical barrier and radial monotonicity assumptions.

metadata.title: Fibrewise Real-Analytic Landsberg Metrics in Dimension at Least Four Are Berwald
metadata.abstract: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge4$, and let $F$ be a smooth, strongly convex Landsberg metric, regular on the entire slit tangent bundle. We prove that $F$ is Berwald if, at each fixed base point, the Minkowski norm is real-analytic on the entire slit tangent space. The proof rests on two analytic rigidity theorems for a single Minkowski space. The first asserts that, in dimension at least $3$, a real-analytic Minkowski norm whose Hessian metric is flat is induced by an inner product. The second asserts that, in dimension at least $4$, the Hessian metric of a real-analytic Minkowski norm is flat if the entire indicatrix carries a nonzero smooth symmetric quartic form satisfying a twisted Codazzi equation. The quartic form need not be real-analytic, and the second theorem is proved independently of the first. Applying these results to the angular Berwald quartic form shows that the metric is Riemannian on the open set of base points on whose fibres the Berwald curvature is not identically zero. Since every Riemannian metric is Berwald, this set must be empty. No analytic structure, compactness or completeness of the base manifold is assumed, and the metric need not be reversible.

metadata.abstract: We study the distortion of the lower dimension and lower spectrum of sets under quasiconformal mappings. metadata.title: An elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity for rank-one planar Lipschitz maps
metadata.abstract: We give an elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity which might be known to specialists in geometric measure theory. It concerns Lipschitz mappings $g$ from the closed unit ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$. Let $x$ be an interior point of differentiability of $g$ at which $Dg(x)$ has rank one. If the upper one-dimensional Hausdorff density of $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ is at most one, then the tangent cone to $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ coincides with the image of $Dg(x)$. This property is used in the proof of rigidity for the four-gradient problem. We provide a detailed, self-contained proof based on differentiability, connectedness and elementary estimates for one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, without using advanced methods from geometric measure theory.

metadata.title: A Smooth Shioda-Tate Isomorphism for Elliptically Fibered 4-Manifolds
metadata.abstract: This paper studies a subgroup of the mapping class group of an elliptically fibered $4$-manifold $\pi: M\to B$, inspired by number theory. The smooth Mordell-Weil group $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ is the group of isotopy classes of smooth sections of $\pi$. We construct a smooth analog of the Shioda-Tate isomorphism, identifying $\mathrm{MW(\pi)}$ with the quotient of $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$ by the trivial lattice of $\pi$. This shows that $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ can be computed explicitly from $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$. As an application, we show that the natural inclusion of the holomorphic Mordell-Weil group into the smooth one is an isomorphism if and only if $M$ is a rational elliptic surface. As another application, we show that $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ satisfies a strong version of Nielsen realization: any torsion element of $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ is represented by a holomorphic translation of $M$ of the same order.

metadata.title: Diastolic inequalities for the distance function min-max width of spheres
metadata.abstract: In this article, we investigate inequalities involving the min-max width associated to the distance function and the area of two-dimensional Riemannian spheres. This geometric invariant naturally arises as min-max methods are applied for the distance function defined on the space of pairs of points. Our methods involve careful constructions of sweepouts that can be performed under the hypothesis that the Riemannian sphere does not contain stable closed geodesics. Improved bounds are obtained under further geometric assumptions (positive curvature, pinching condition, and antipodal symmetry). In the cases of a pinching condition or antipodal symmetry, our inequalities are optimal.

metadata.title: Convex ribbon disks, quasipositivity, and Lagrangian sliceness
metadata.abstract: We introduce a version of convex surface theory for immersed ribbon surfaces with Legendrian boundary. As an application, we establish a special case of K3: Problem 1.70 on sharpness in the slice-Bennequin inequality implying quasipositivity, and a special case of a conjecture of Cornwell, Ng, and Sivek on characterizing Lagrangian sliceness. Specifically, we prove that if $K$ is a knot that bounds a "star-shaped" ribbon disk and satisfies $\overline{\mathrm{sl}}(K) = -1$ (resp.\ $\overline{\mathrm{tb}}(K) = -1$), then $K$ is quasipositive (resp.\ Lagrangian slice). In fact, we prove these statements for any fixed transverse (resp.\ Legendrian) representative.

metadata.title: Morse accessibility with applications to Coxeter groups
metadata.abstract: In this paper we begin developing a theory of Morse hierarchies for finitely generated groups. Very roughly, a Morse hierarchy is a iterative splitting of a group over subgroups that do not contribute to the Morse boundary of the ambient group. We apply this theory to Coxeter groups, establishing new combinatorial criteria that distinguish certain Coxeter groups from other Coxeter groups as well as right-angled Artin groups up to quasi-isometry. We highlight the consequences for the right-angled case. To build the reader's intuition, the last section provides many examples of Morse hierarchies and their subtleties. Finally, there is an appendix by the second author and Vivian He that extends these ideas to the metrizable Cashen--Mackay topology on the Morse boundary.

analysisBasis.abstract: In this paper we begin developing a theory of Morse hierarchies for finitely generated groups. Very roughly, a Morse hierarchy is a iterative splitting of a group over subgroups that do not contribute to the Morse boundary of the ambient group. We apply this theory to Coxeter groups, establishing new combinatorial criteria that distinguish certain Coxeter groups from other Coxeter groups as well as right-angled Artin groups up to quasi-isometry. We highlight the consequences for the right-angled case. To build the reader's intuition, the last section provides many examples of Morse hierarchies and their subtleties. Finally, there is an appendix by the second author and Vivian He that extends these ideas to the metrizable Cashen--Mackay topology on the Morse boundary.

metadata.title: Toric gravitational instantons with four fixed points
metadata.abstract: We classify the simply connected toric gravitational instantons whose torus action has four fixed points. They are the hyperkähler multi-Eguchi--Hanson and multi-Taub--NUT metrics with four collinear centres, the asymptotically flat instantons on Li and Sun's manifold $X_3$, up to scale one for each twist at infinity in $(0,1)$ for a fixed orientation of the torus, and, up to scale, a single further instanton with an ALF end, which is not hyperkähler. The last two are Hermitian for neither orientation. In particular, the toric asymptotically flat instanton on $X_3$ with a given twist is unique up to scale, as conjectured by Li and Sun. The proof combines the solitonic form of Geroch's conjecture, which turns smoothness into polynomial equations for the soliton data, with a convexity principle adapted from Aksteiner. At a fixed asymptotic parameter, the cone errors of the conical metrics with a given rod structure are the gradient of a strictly convex function of the rod lengths, and the strict convexity gives uniqueness. Existence follows from an explicit solution for the ALF end and, for the AF ends, from Li and Sun's existence theorem. We also outline how a chart of Aksteiner identifies these AF instantons with those found by Teo.
